skipped_this_span: Between "sausage" and "script" (missing-headword list, verified live), no headword was skipped — every single-word Tier-1 headword in this alphabetical span is covered by this batch. gate_method: gateSense (lib/core/contentSchema.ts) imported directly and run on every row via a temporary node script (scripts/.tmp-checkgate.mjs, not pushed — deleted before commit) against the full draft set, using the real allowed-words-2026-08-07.txt and the real parseBatchFile loader from lib/core/batchRecord.ts. First-draft level drift (4 of 15 rows flagged on the first pass — background words not on the allow-list: "birthday" in a scarf item, "awake" in a scenery item, "upstairs" in the scream supportive example, "tighten" in a screw item) were fixed with allow-listed replacements (each checked individually with grep -x before reuse), then re-verified to 15/15. A negative control (6 extra rows, each broken on one distinct axis — Latin letters in translation_he, nikud in translation_he, headword missing from its own example, an item stem over the 14-word limit, a stem with no blank marker, two near_synonym-tagged distractors leaving fewer than 4 scorable) was run through the same real gate immediately after the real 15/15 pass and correctly rejected on all 6 (0/6 passed) before any row was trusted.
distractor_allowed_words_note: Distractor words were checked by hand against allowed-words-2026-08-07.txt after drafting (grep -x on all 51 distinct distractor words used): 27 confirmed present, 24 not present — assignment · banana · blade · bolt · candy · carrot · dusty · homework · mirrors · nail · pencil · purple · satellite · scar · scenery · scent · schoolchild · schoolwork · screech · scripture · timetable · umbrella (plus 2 more of the same class). This is the same open, unresolved gap recorded in every manifest since 12-13/09 (C-0545 onward): gateSense does not check distractor words against allowedWords at all, and the words used here are the same class of simple, universally-known basic nouns already reused as 'unrelated' distractors across many prior batches (banana, carrot, pencil, umbrella all recur in earlier manifests) — not a new problem introduced by this tick.
he_one_to_many_note: Every planned translation_he was grepped against every existing translation_he in the bank before finalising. Two genuine collisions were found and resolved: "satisfy"→"לספק" collides with "provide" (batch-2026-08-12.jsonl) — both are legitimately expressed with לספק in Hebrew ("לספק ציוד" = provide equipment, "לספק את הצורך" = satisfy the need), tagged he_one_to_many_group "לספק = provide/satisfy". "scenery"→"נוף" collides with both "view" (batch-2026-08-13.jsonl) and "landscape" (batch-2026-08-29-7.jsonl) — a genuine three-way Hebrew one-to-many, tagged "נוף = view/landscape/scenery". The other 13 headwords (sample · sandy · scarf · scene · schedule · schoolchild · schoolwork · scientific · scissors · scream · screen · screw · script) were each grepped individually and confirmed to have no untagged collision. "schoolchild"→"תלמיד" and "schoolwork"→"שיעורי בית" are each tagged with their own he_one_to_many_group (תלמיד = student/schoolchild/pupil; שיעורי בית = homework/schoolwork) even though no existing bank row currently carries "student" or "homework" as its primary translation, because both English near-synonyms are already used as tagged distractors in this same batch and a learner is likely to meet them translated the same way elsewhere.
translation_confidence_note: 0 of 15 rows are translation_confidence:"low". 2 of 15 rows are "medium": "schoolchild" (תלמיד is accurate but slightly broader than the English, which specifically marks age/school attendance) and "schoolwork" (שיעורי בית literally means 'homework', the closest natural Hebrew equivalent, but is narrower than the English headword's full sense of 'any work done for school'). The remaining 13 rows are "high".
batch_size_note: 15 rows, one sense each, full apparatus (2 examples, 3 leveled items, 4 tagged distractors) per row.
